business: SpeakCheck — iPhone app: IELTS Speaking and job-interview pronunciation trainer for Russian speakers
target: Russian-speaking iPhone owners in Bishkek, 17 to 35, with an IELTS Speaking test or an English job interview in the next 1–3 months
where: Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan (App Store KG, prices shown in USD)

segments.name: Student preparing IELTS to study abroad (family pays or part-time job)
Working professional needing IELTS for relocation or a master's
Job seeker preparing an English interview (IT, outsourcing, international org)

behaviours.name: Already pays a course or tutor
behaviours.how: Pays an IELTS centre or tutor in Bishkek ($50–140 a month) and adds apps only if the teacher recommends them.

behaviours.name: Free-only
behaviours.how: Uses free tiers, YouTube and ChatGPT voice; cancels every trial before it charges.

behaviours.name: Burned by another app
behaviours.how: Tried ELSA or Praktika, hit crashes, mic problems or a surprise paywall, and is now suspicious of subscriptions.

behaviours.name: Last-minute crammer
behaviours.how: Exam or interview is in 2–3 weeks; will pay for anything that clearly helps right now, then stop.

behaviours.name: Asks the Telegram chat first
behaviours.how: Checks what people in IELTS Telegram groups recommend before installing anything.

behaviours.name: Deal hunter
behaviours.how: Waits for a discount or a yearly plan with a big saving before paying.

behaviours.name: Self-learner
behaviours.how: Studies alone every evening with a plan; likes tracking progress and streaks.

objections: Another subscription — I already pay for a course
Pronunciation is only one of four IELTS criteria; I need fluency, vocabulary and grammar too
Can an app really score my pronunciation accurately?
ChatGPT voice mode is free and can also correct me
Apps like this crash or don't hear the microphone
My tutor already corrects my pronunciation
Paying in USD through the App Store feels expensive in soms
habits: you study on your phone in the marshrutka on the way to university or work
you are in two or three IELTS Telegram chats
you watch English YouTube videos with Russian subtitles
you practise speaking answers alone in your room before the exam
your English reading is fine, but you freeze when you have to speak
